private_note: My household lands in the fourth fifth no matter what, so it's just the numbers: Cedar 122, Today 108, Alder 106, Birch 90, Hazel 86. Cedar is a long shot for nine votes, and a failed convention leaves me at 108 anyway, so I lose nothing by holding out. Alder costs me only 2, so I could live with it if it gathers a real coalition. Birch and Hazel cut me by 18 to 22. I block those.
statement: I run a heating and cooling business with six people on the payroll. Most of what my wife and I have is tied up in that business. I'm going to be straight with you: I'm voting for what keeps my household and my business healthy. Cedar grows the whole economy the most, and that growth is what keeps small firms like mine hiring. Birch and Hazel shrink the economy by a fifth. They would take a big bite out of households like mine, and out of the businesses that employ the second and middle groups. I won't support either of them. Remember the rules: if no plan gets nine votes, we keep what we have today. So any plan that wants my vote has to leave me better off than the status quo, or very close to it. I'm listening for proposals that pass that test.
